notes: San Francisco Bay Guardian, 1998 to 2006, 122 issues in the Internet Archive collection, read from its DjVu text. Hand-curated: news-word passages, article clusters and event passages were read and each finding's quote checked against the issue. People rule as in the dossier: no owners, staff, tenants, performers or customers; landlords in the housing stories are not named.

coverage.remaining: 395 issues, 2008 to 2014 (lower value: those years were on the open web).
coverage.note: 122 issues; 93,929 numbered-address mentions on EAS streets, of which the advertisement filter marked 82,283 and kept 2,688 windows in 2,122 address clusters. Read in full: the 85 passages of the news-word pass over the raw text, the 91 clusters of article prose, and the 62 event-word passages for places printed without a number. The 373 event-word clusters under the tighter filter were not read. About 60 candidates were checked against the issue text; 40 were written and 1 dropped, Temple Beautiful at 1839 Geary, already on its page from the 1979 issue. Not entered: an eviction case and three houses with private residents, two places printed without a number, and a live-work project whose number is doubtful in the scan. 39 findings, each quote found again in the issue's text. 22 resolved and published on 22 existing pages. 8 held as single facts on parcels with no page (444 Battery, 595 Castro, 360 10th, 575 Harrison, 1207 Indiana, 1600 Webster, 1335 Webster, 1547 Clay). 9 unresolved because EAS no longer has the address: 699 Columbus, 960 Bush, 2520 Third, 965 Market, 81 Third, 6114 California, 2955 18th, 1300 Sutter and 701 Lombard. Eleven findings come from one retrospective article of June 2000 on the punk scene of the 1970s and are dated to the events it describes. Framed as site history: 980 Howard, 3620 19th, 960 Bush, 699 Columbus.
